Water damage is one of those problems where a single sensor can save you a significant amount of money on repairs to floors, cabinets, and more. Leak sensors have long been one of the best-value products in the smart home category, and Shelly's new Flood S Gen4 makes getting started even easier. It's priced under $30, Matter-certified, and works with Apple Home right out of the box.

The HomeKit Weekly column is a series dedicated to smart home accessories, automation tips, and everything related to the Apple smart home framework.

Larger sensing surface area

Most leak sensors on the market use small metal probes on the bottom, which means water has to pool in exactly the right spot to trigger an alarm. Shelly's new sensor takes a completely different approach, featuring three large stainless steel sensing pads on the bottom of the device. The larger contact area means it can detect water faster and in more locations—precisely matching the reason you'd place a sensor under a water heater or washing machine.

These sensing pads are also sensitive enough to detect clean or low-conductivity water, such as condensation from air conditioners. This type of leak is typically harder to spot. The Flood S Gen4 is also slim enough to slide under appliances, behind toilets, and under sinks—all exactly the places you'd want to put a device like this.

Matter / Apple Home support

The Flood S Gen4 is Matter-certified and supports both Wi-Fi and Zigbee, so it works with Apple Home, Google Home, Amazon Alexa, SmartThings, and Home Assistant. Once added to Apple Home, automation possibilities expand significantly:

  • Cut power to the washing machine or dishwasher the moment water is detected (if connected to a smart plug)
  • Trigger every smart bulb in the house
  • Simply and directly push leak alerts to your iPhone (especially useful when you're not home)

Modes, alerts, and battery life

Beyond phone notifications, the device has a built-in local alarm that will be heard even if someone's phone is in another room. Shelly offers two operating modes—Flood Detection and Rain Detection—plus three alert settings (High, Normal, and Economy), letting you strike a balance between leak detection speed and battery life. The device runs on the included CR123A battery and can last up to two years.

Wrap-up

At under $30, this is the kind of accessory that makes it a no-brainer to grab three or four. In front of the water heater, in front of the dishwasher, under the washing machine, and under the kitchen sink—all deserve one. Matter / Apple Home support lets you receive alerts through the Home app and build Apple Home automations around it. This product has a lot going for it, and I can't find a single downside. Trust me—a leak sensor is absolutely the smartest investment you can make for your smart home.

You can purchase the Flood S Gen4 on Amazon or directly from Shelly.
